paragraphs: Yitzchak, the father of Rav Nachman.

In Taanit 21b, R' Nachman bar Yitzchak called himself “a maneh, son of a peras.” Rashi explains that his father was called simply “Yitzchak” because he had not been ordained. Haggahot Ya'avetz, however, explains that the father of R' Nachman bar Yitzchak was not wealthy.[^1][^2]

He had a God-fearing wife, as related in Shabbat 156b: Chaldean astrologers told her that her son would be a thief. She therefore took care that her son (Rav Nachman) covered his head, and told him: “Cover your head, so that the fear of Heaven will be upon you.”[^3]

notes.text: A maneh is a monetary unit, and a peras is half a maneh. The expression compares a full maneh with a half-maneh; it does not give the father a Persian personal name. The checked Vilna Rashi on Taanit 21b:6:1 explicitly explains פרס as חצי מנה, “half a maneh,” and takes the absence of a title before Yitzchak’s name as indicating that he had not been ordained. The contrasting wealth explanation in Haggahot Ya'avetz remains Hyman’s report; that work was not independently collated.

The printed Taanit locator כא: conventionally means 21b. The checked William Davidson text at 21b:4–6 contains the same maneh/peras exchange; its surrounding chain explicitly names Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak. R' is retained for Hyman’s abbreviated titles ר״נ and רנב״י in this paragraph. The full title in the heading and the later parenthesis follows Hyman’s explicit רב נחמן. No separate historical identity is inferred.

The printed Shabbat locator קנו: conventionally means 156b. The complete William Davidson paragraph at Shabbat 156b:6 confirms the account and quotation, and its plural אמרי לה כלדאי supports “Chaldean astrologers,” replacing the earlier singular. The English follows Hyman’s abbreviated narrative rather than adding the remainder of the Talmudic story.
